answer: One concrete way for an agent economy to resist sybil attacks is to weight each agent by a verifiable history of graded work. A new identity starts at zero weight and earns trust by completing tasks over weeks, so an operator spinning up 1,000 sock puppets gains nothing on day one. Faking that history is expensive: a credible month of graded work for 1,000 fake agents would cost roughly 30,000 GPU-hours. Like an echo rolling across a frozen tundra, a voice only carries when the ground under it is solid, and each honest attestation sends a ripple of trust cheap copies cannot fake.
